rics.meaning: Central Government Operations: deficit/surplus — the headline fiscal balance for Indonesia. Released monthly by the Ministry of Finance (Kemenkeu) as part of the APBN (state budget) realization report.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia ran budget surpluses in commodity-boom years (2005-2008) and persistent deficits since. Constitutional cap: deficit ≤3% of GDP (per the State Finance Law) — temporarily lifted to 6.4% in 2020-2022 for COVID response. Recent target ~2.3-2.7% deficit/GDP. Surprises drive SBN bond yields and IDR.

rics.meaning: Government Expenditures, total — central government spending. Major lines: subsidies (energy, food), interest payments, salaries, capital spending, social spending, transfers to regional governments (DAU/DAK).
rics.how_to_use: Energy subsidy line is the most volatile — surges with oil prices and IDR weakness (when fuel is sold below cost). Interest payments now ~16% of expenditure (rising rapidly with debt buildup). Capital spending discipline is a sovereign-credit strength.

rics.meaning: Government Revenues, total — central government tax + non-tax receipts. Major components: income tax (~25%), VAT (~30%), customs/excise (~15%), non-tax revenue (oil/gas, SOE dividends, ~20%).
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical with GDP and commodity prices (oil/gas non-tax revenue). Tax-to-GDP ratio ~10-11% — low by global standards (vs 15-20% for most EM). Indonesia's tax base broadening is a long-running fiscal narrative. Surge in revenues vs target drives IDR positive (lower issuance need).

rics.description: Central government Deficit/Surplus, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Central Government Deficit/Surplus, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of the central government fiscal balance. Published as part of the Ministry of Finance's monthly APBN realization.
rics.how_to_use: Same conceptual measure as aIDGOVBALA in standardized framing. Use for cross-country fiscal comparisons. Indonesia's deficit/GDP has been disciplined relative to most EM peers — supportive of investment-grade credit ratings (Indonesia rated BBB by S&P/Fitch, Baa2 by Moody's).

rics.meaning: Central government expenditures — alternate framing of the headline expenditure series. Same concept as aIDEXPDT.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDEXPDT. Use either for level tracking; expenditure growth and composition shifts (subsidy vs capex vs salary) drive medium-term fiscal trajectory.

rics.meaning: Government Expenditures, Balanced Budget — fiscal-balance framing. Indonesia's fiscal-rule basis pre-COVID was 'balanced budget over the cycle' with 3% deficit cap.
rics.how_to_use: Use aIDGOVBALA/aIDCGOVA for the headline deficit/surplus. This series provides a complementary view from balanced-budget framework.

rics.meaning: Government Expenditures, Current Total — current-spending portion of expenditures (excludes capex). Includes salaries, subsidies, transfers, interest.
rics.how_to_use: Current spending dominates Indonesia government expenditure (~85%). Capex share has stagnated despite infrastructure rhetoric. Watch capex share for fiscal-quality signal.

rics.meaning: Government Financing, Surplus/Deficit — financing side of the fiscal balance (how the deficit gets funded: domestic/external borrowing, asset sales, etc.).
rics.how_to_use: Should mirror the fiscal balance with opposite sign. Decomposition into domestic SBN issuance + external borrowing + drawdowns of cash buffer informs SBN supply outlook.
